item.description:
One of our members supports theatre projects with custom technical gadgets. This unusual-looking device recently received an update: it is a remote-controlled vehicle equipped with moving-head LED lights for creating special effects.

A particularly useful feature is its direct support for DMX, the protocol commonly used to control lighting equipment in theatre productions.

item.title: One of our member build a small turret orchestra inspired by Portal 2. Each…
item.description:
One of our member build a small turret orchestra inspired by Portal 2.

Each turret is driven by a solenoid switched through a solid state relay. Conductive copper strips and 3D printed spring contacts make the units hot-swappable, while a Pi plays a MIDI file and the original audio at the same time, triggering each turret based on its assigned note.

#hackerspace #makerspace #openworkshop #MunichMakerLab #MuMaLab #Kreativquartier #Kreativlabor #DIYMunich #portal2 #midi #raspberrypi

item.title: Soil discovery at the Kreativlabor site – a scientific report In 2016,…
item.description:
Soil discovery at the Kreativlabor site – a scientific report

In 2016, researchers from the Technical University of Munich identified unusually high concentrations of semiconductor metals, precious metals, and previously unknown energy sources in the ground of today's Munich Maker Lab.

A perfect habitat for a makerspace.

Take a closer look at the soil model on site and explore the distinct layers yourself.

item.title: Terry is currently working on a “Jeticopter” and wrote a blog post about it:…
item.description:
Terry is currently working on a “Jeticopter” and wrote a blog post about it:

This is a blog post that I’ve written for Jetex.org. this site is for enthusiasts of free flying model planes powered by long duration, solid fuel rocket motors. this is a technology founded in the UK around 1950 and most readers are unacquainted with such technologies as 3D printing and CAD design. Rather models are made of balsa wood and doped tissue paper and inherently stable. In these blog posts I’m trying to introduce the audience to some different ways of doing things!

item.title: We recently had a bunch of students from TuM over to build an automated chess…
item.description:
We recently had a bunch of students from TuM over to build an automated chess board. 

We are Team One, one of the many teams that took part in the soft and hard skills program Adveisor in 2021, organized by the Chair of Control and Automation Engineering at the Technical University of Munich. In this project we worked together as a team and built a remote controlled self-playing chessboard.
We would like to thank the @MunichMakerLab for the great support during the project and for providing workplaces.

Check out the project website or talk to Spacezhang on our Slack to learn more.

Just getting started? We offer a range of courses and introductions to get you started. Sign up today!

item.title: Jan built a camera robot that holds a smartphone and points its camera at…
item.description:
Jan built a camera robot that holds a smartphone and points its camera at things.

It consists of a stepper motor, a roller bearing, an oversized power supply and a servo. It is controlled using an ESP8266 and an old 3D printer controller board.

The smartphone then sends a live video feed to his PC to be used as a secondary webcam.

Here is a video of it in use: https://www.twitch.tv/jvpeek/clip/HardEncouragingFriesSMOrc-huGqPbwWFnrbcqyL

item.title: The other day, one of our network switches broken, and just wouldn’t turn on.…
item.description: The other day, one of our network switches broken, and just wouldn’t turn on. We had a replacement in storage, but couldn’t get us to throw the old one out. Turns out it was just a broken capacitor, which is a 5 minutes, 20cents fix. After replacing the broken one, the whole thing works again. So now we have a new replacement switch when the next one breaks 😁

Hey there!

Just a heads up from us: We’re still alive, but the lab is in a bit of corona-related hibernation. Current restrictions mean our physical space has to be closed to everyone, even our members. We’re trying to organize some virtual events, some of our regular meetups have moved to virtual formats, and we’re kicking off a new electronics meetup next week. You can check out our calendar for all the events.

In the meantime, here’s a sneak peek at our attempt to create a 3D scan of the space for all of you who miss us so dearly. Well, let’s just say we’re not quite there yet 😅
